actions.findings:
Irreducible autocatalytic subnetworks are formally characterized by algebraic conditions on stoichiometric submatrices, enabling persistent, history-dependent states. [peer-0592c13110957d2468eeda39]

Heritable information involves pattern inheritance that is structurally and functionally distinct from mere dissipative non-equilibrium persistence. [peer-0ddbaefa42da4c9696f793ed]
actions.limitations: Theoretical formulations of stoichiometric submatrices require empirical verification in non-equilibrium flow reactor environments to confirm functional persistence. Current evidence provides structural bounds rather than exhaustive experimental confirmation of transition thresholds.
actions.next_questions: What precise perturbations differentiate state-holding persistence from template-copying in high-fidelity chemical networks? Can we engineer a system to transition between these states?
actions.reason: Revision necessary to integrate algebraic criteria for autocatalytic persistence into the heredity transition framework.
actions.summary: This revision formalizes the distinction between irreducible autocatalytic networks, which support persistent history-dependent states via stoichiometric constraints, and template-directed heredity, which requires discrete inheritance mechanisms. Evidence suggests that while autocatalytic persistence provides a substrate for chemical memory, it is distinct from the information-copying fidelity required for Darwinian evolution.
actions.title: Experimental Distinctions Between Autocatalytic Memory and Template-Directed Heredity

proposal.summary: This journal entry synthesizes findings regarding the formal algebraic conditions for autocatalytic chemical memory and evaluates the structural transition to heritable information in non-equilibrium systems.
proposal.title: Synthesis of Autocatalytic Chemical Memory and Heredity Thresholds
